title: PSX souls-like with Opus
author: wormsparty5
selftext:
My new favoring thing is asking Opus to create PSX-styles games. I had a lot of fun making this and I like the end result.

Playable here with 7 bosses: [https://wormsparty.github.io/psx-souls/](https://wormsparty.github.io/psx-souls/)

Code here: [https://github.com/wormsparty/psx-souls/](https://github.com/wormsparty/psx-souls/)

comments.body: This is adorable. Loving the idea here

comments.author: nebetsu
comments.body: Just wondering \~ how much does it cost to generate something like this? Could you break it down if there are extra charges for lots of tokens for someone who might want to get into doing stuff like this?

replies.author: wormsparty5
replies.body: Not much. I have the Claude 20$ plan, and the initial prompt took about 30 minutes with Opus-5.5 to have the first arena with a playable boss. After that, I prompted a few more iterations and it worked for about 4 hours where I had a 2 checkpoint, a small map, ennemies on the map, pickable items, etc. After that I iterated some more for a few days to polish the balancing, add an ending, you can see the timeline in the list of commits: [https://github.com/wormsparty/psx-souls/commits/main/](https://github.com/wormsparty/psx-souls/commits/main/)

replies.author: nebetsu
replies.body: Noice! Thank you for your response!

replies.author: wormsparty5
replies.body:
Let's say the real skill is prompting. Test what works and what doesn't. Like if you take my project and ask "Make a PS2-looking version of this", it doesn't work. You would have to have a smart plan for this. I still have a screenshot: background look really nice but the character upgrade looks really ugly

replies.author: wormsparty5
replies.body:
I don't have the original prompt of this project, but to get you started here's the sort of prompt I make:

I’d like to start a new project: a Resident Evil-style game with the aesthetic of the original PlayStation era. Please write it in Rust, with the ability to compile it to WASM for a web application. For this initial version, I’d like the following features: A female protagonist controlled using modern mechanics for this genre (left/right turns the character, while the stick allows for free movement). Support for both gamepads and keyboard/mouse controls. The setting is a dark mansion; create a few rooms. There is no way to exit, but the outside is visible through the windows—darkness, the moon in the distance, and mountains. The mansion is surrounded by swamp-like vegetation and the sound of barking dogs. Include the ability to move between rooms and pick up items, such as a key to open a door and a health kit. Add a weapon that can be drawn to shoot zombies—using limited ammo found in the game—and a checkpoint system. Please ask any questions you need to, then proceed with the implementation.
